title: Packing Services in Santa Clarita | SOS Moving
metaDescription: Packing services in Santa Clarita, CA: hourly SOS crews for Newhall, Canyon Country and Valencia homes, boxes from $4 billed by use, free tape and wrap.
heroSubtitle: Room-by-room packing for Santa Clarita homes, old and new: you pay only for the boxes the crew fills, and tape and stretch wrap cost nothing.

faq.question: Why can a packing job in Santa Clarita have a 4-hour minimum?
faq.answer: Our standard minimum is 3 hours, but an address 30 or more miles from the Los Angeles base carries a 4-hour minimum. Drive time beyond 10 miles is also billed at double. The estimator checks your exact address, so the quote shows which rule applies.

faq.question: Can you pack on a weekend in an HOA with quiet hours?
faq.answer: Yes. We work Monday – Sunday, 8AM – 6PM, and on weekend mornings we can hold box assembly and taping until the association's guideline allows it, such as the 9 a.m. weekend mark at Valencia Lakeshore. Packed cartons stay inside your home or garage, not on shared walkways.

faq.question: Where do the boxes and bubble wrap go after unpacking?
faq.answer: Under Burrtec's rules for city homes, flattened cardboard goes loose in the recycling barrel, and tape and labels may stay on. Bubble wrap, shrink wrap and packing peanuts are not accepted curbside and go in the garbage. Boxes in good shape are worth keeping for the next move.

faq.question: Should I get rid of furniture before the packers come?
faq.answer: It saves crew hours, because we never pack what you plan to throw away. Residents can book a free Burrtec bulky-item pickup at least 48 hours before their regular collection day, up to four times a year and three items each time. Pick a collection day before packing day so the driveway is clear for the truck.

faq.question: Can I pack some rooms myself and leave the fragile ones to you?
faq.answer: Yes, partial packing is a standard option. The crew takes the kitchen, glassware, mirrors and art, and you box books, clothes and linens. Jewelry, documents and other valuables should travel with you either way.
